# SystemUI islands and media

Part of the [feature reference](../features.md). Search by feature or class name and read only the matching section.

## Island ownership and geometry

- Island hook assembly lives in `IslandHookPlan`, separate from `IslandHookContext`. `IslandRuntime` constructs the per-generation coordinators; `IslandSessionState` retains the single session registry, callback scopes and projections, and publishes typed `*Actions` capabilities. Binders and coordinators consume this state and ports without importing the composition root or another coordinator implementation. Native target discovery, install order, setting refresh and saved-owner migration stay in the existing ThreeIsland lifecycle. The mode gate (`enabled`/`phoneEligible`/`flags`) reads orientation, slot readiness and phone eligibility through reflection; read-only coordinate and region callbacks wrap their body in `IslandSessionState.readOnlyGate`, which reuses one snapshot of those host facts per owner. Preferences, retirement and session health are always read fresh. Never open that scope around code that changes slots, handlers or windows.
- Island geometry ownership: the scheduling session (row admission, settle, frame relayout, full templates) is enabled only by three islands / landscape full / landscape more. Placeholder removal is a stateless per-view rewrite in `CompactCoordinator`: it handles every camera-seated asymmetric main template, keyed by the content view rather than the current handler, so expand, hide and exit animations keep the width they started with. Its translation is applied only when the `doBigIslandAnim` field set matches the presented geometry. A full template that leaves the row (HIDDEN/OTHER) keeps its lease and offset until the matching `DynamicIslandAnimationDelegate` lifecycle FINISH/CANCEL tag, or a timeout. Promotion to BIG or EXPANDED releases it at once. The hook plan stays uninstalled until any island switch is on. App close: the host hands WM the BIG rect at `request_close_position` and re-measures at `close_app_start`; the fake view pre-scales by screen / new width while the window shrinks into the old rect, so a width change in between (HyperLyrics Enhanced showing its injected lyric views, which fill `AT_MOST(screen/2)` areas) shrinks the content to old/new. The width changes both ways (lyrics appear 258→714 or hide 714→258). `AppCloseWidthBinder` pins the view's stored nine geometry fields (`NativeIslandHost.storedResult`), which the close rect is read from, when they match the rect WM received; a module-published result is not used because another module may rewrite those fields. It returns them for re-measures until `updateViewStateWhenCloseEnd` (1.5 s timeout), then calls `updateBigIslandViewWidth` if a re-measure was held. A live media-return projection is never pinned. Keep the helper result hook at default priority: running it outside HyperLyrics' width hook defeats that module's content barrier and delays the cover. Owner tracking is always installed. A settings refresh resets session health and re-measures compact views. Module budgets cap each measured template at the host `maxWidth`, because the host measures areas with `AT_MOST(screen/2)` and lyric templates fill it. While Duo is enabled, they also remove SystemUI's 8dp charging allowance from the battery reservation; the bolt sits inside the Duo icon. The charging state is snapshotted when the host publishes its status widths (the base view's `(F,F,F)` writer), using SystemUI's rule: plugged in and status charging or full.
  Mode eligibility and native recovery are separate. Portrait scheduling requires three islands; landscape accepts the matching switches. Keyless views never enter the module scheduler. However, keyless BIG or SMALL pointers must not permanently lock out recovery: `SettlementCoordinator.reconcileNative` runs before native handler publication and before explicit relayout. It reads the window's authoritative living content registry plus native slots/queue, rejects rebuild/expanded/show-once/temp-show ownership, and releases keyless visible-slot pointers while leaving native queue markers alone. Native `handleFillInState` repairs the affected slot; a valid BIG is preserved when only SMALL needs repair. Registered summary tasks missing from all handlers/queue are readmitted through native arbitration. Non-null marker states, non-summary/Deleted states and unknown data are not rewritten. Recovery never flushes the host list itself, so event publication keeps its original stop boundary. `CallbackContext.withNativeSession` carries the owner across the entire native event, including nested animation scopes: EventCoordinator stops through AppStateHandler, which is not one of the five island slot handlers. Matching only those slots misses native collapse. The owner scope is restored on return/exception and does not create a scheduling transaction.
  `NativeIslandDiscovery` schema 2 resolves the ordinary native admission path by its semantic log anchor, three-operand signature and handler/content type relationships. It must not confuse the identically shaped tiny-screen path. Native refill is the unique ArrayList-to-content virtual shape also called by deletion; inventory is the verified window content-list getter. All methods resolve before callbacks are installed.
  All module-driven island measurements go through `IslandSessionState.measure`: content identity, a non-null task key, and both real template areas are required. `calculateBigIslandWidth` is destructive on an unbound view: its missing-area branch invokes native `removeByError`, removes children and clears state. Never measure the native queue's Empty marker, even when refreshing hidden/expanded content. Reconciliation removes already-corrupted keyless non-Empty queue entries and updates the hidden pointer before native refill; valid Empty ordering markers remain native-owned.
  Restoration revokes module frames, template leases, gesture/seat history and media-return projections. Explicit settings/hot-reload/configuration relayout then reconciles ownership, measures and publishes one native addState/stop batch after the new layout, with the config-change flag saved/restored. This publication also runs with row scheduling disabled: width measurement alone cannot restore the root alpha, clip or container translation that native configuration transitions change. Do not replace complete state restoration with `alpha=1` or another coordinate patch.
  Placeholder removal remains a per-view camera-template measurement owner. Full-template cleanup cannot overwrite its lease, and scheduled geometry loses projection authority when its mode turns off. Native coordinate getters are only overridden by a live module row/media projection. The old `MainFrameJournal`, first-event priming and historical-edge/native-small-target fallbacks were removed; invalid native ownership is repaired before animation publication instead of inventing a destination. DUMP diagnostics include raw native slots, the complete living registry and queue, not only filtered summaries; tracing remains bounded to 60s/500 phase events and never captures pixels or operates UI. Per-frame properties require explicit `trace_frames=true`; default traces preserve the whole event sequence.
- Released camera padding and the island timer font. A media/camera-releasing lease zeroes the template's camera-side inner padding, but the host's `IslandTemplateFactory.updateLeftWidth`/`updateRightWidth(data, int, isFake)` still pass a width that the holder's `updateWidth` reduces by that padding. The before-hook on those writers adds the released padding back for the factory whose content view holds the lease. Without it, a narrowed timer overflows by a few px, and `IslandSameWidthDigitViewHolder` applies its fixed 0.79 digit scale instead of narrowing the pill. `IslandTimeFontHooker` swaps the font at `setFixedFont`, inside the holder's own width pass. It records each holder's last `updateWidth` budget, which survives hot reload. When a settings refresh or `updatePartial` changes a font outside that pass, it re-runs `updateWidth(budget)` and then the owning `DynamicIslandBaseContentView.calculateBigIslandWidth()`, which re-measures the areas and applies the layout. `IslandFixedWidthDigitViewHolder` sizes from the fixed `island_fixed_width` resource, so the narrow font cannot shrink those templates.
- Island pull-down stretch (`IslandPullDownHooker`, plugin session). The fake view's private `onFakeViewTrackingParamsUpdated()` runs for every drag frame and every Folme rebound frame. Its `FakeViewTrackingParams` give the outline height (`bottom - top`, growing from `mFakeViewHeight`) and `alpha` (1 down to 0 toward the mini-window trigger). Each frame is derived from those alone (`IslandPullDownFrame`): the children of `getFakeExpandedView()` scale from the top to the outline, capped at 1.6, and blur through the host's static `setMiSelfBlurCompat`, at 40 × progress while background material is open. The container keeps its own outline and blur. `ExpandedTracker.updateTrack(F)` sends `pull_down_action_offset_y`, which only the SystemUI media binder consumes, to slide its album background. While the switch is on, that offset is published as 0. The captured transforms are restored at the rest frame, `onTrackingFakeViewStart`, `onTrackingFakeViewReset`, `resetFakeViewState`, detach, a non-visible `setVisibility`, disable and hot reload. The fake view is hidden once the mini window takes over, so the stretch holds until then.
- Island Lottie resume (`IslandLottieResumeHooker`, plugin session). The `DynamicIslandEventCoordinator` `AnimEventBridge` listener (`initAnimEventBridge$1`) pauses or resets each island key's Lottie scenes (`LottieProgressManager.pauseForIslandAnim`) on `onAnimTrulyStarted`, and replays them on the next `onAnimTrulyFinished`/`onAnimCancelled`, but only while `lottiePausedByAnim` is set. When a second transition starts before the first reports completion, and has no pauses pending, the host clears the flag without resuming. `pausedLottieKeys` stays filled, so a collapsed timer or stopwatch icon holds frame 0. While the switch is on, an after-hook on `onAnimTrulyStarted` sets the flag again whenever paused keys are outstanding, so the host's own resume runs when the bridge's last animation ends. The hooker keeps no state. Keys orphaned before the switch was enabled resume after the next island transition.
- Island flashlight panel (`IslandFlashlightHooker`, plugin session, plus `FlashlightIslandRetentionHooker` on the SystemUI loader). Before `DynamicIslandWindowViewController.add/updateDynamicIslandView`, the flashlight entry (sbn package `miui.systemui.plugin`, channel `flashlight_channel`, focus `param_v2.business == "miui_flashlight"`) gets `FlashlightIslandPanel` as `view` and a second, non-interactive panel as `fakeView`; the big and small islands keep their template. The panel is the plugin's own flashlight page: `layout/mi_flashlight_layout` inflated with the plugin class loader (body container, `mi_seekbar_bg` track, `MiVerticalSeekBar`), its `mi_fl_view` stub replaced by `layout/mi_flashlight_static_effect` with the `mi_flash_low_close` / `mi_flash_long_light` / `mi_flash_compose_light` bitmaps, which is the effect `MiFlashlightUiFolme` installs (the OpenGL `FlashlightRender` is not reused). The page (`mi_flashlight_layout`) is laid out at display size and scaled uniformly to fill the width of a 200×320dp card on black (a narrower page leaves strips, because the shader's dark base is not pure black), with the slider container's bottom 6dp above a 26dp strip kept for the island's `mini_window_bar` pull handle; the head is the page centre in both renderers. Its `mi_fl_view` stub is replaced as the page does it: the real panel runs the plugin's OpenGL `FlashlightRender` on a `miuix.mgl.android.GLTextureView` (progress = `updateFlashlightUi`, never below 0.15 while lit), the fake copy uses the low-end static layers, because `MglContext` is a per-process singleton that every new surface resets. The GL contract (renderer is an `MglRenderer`, view is a `TextureView`, `attachToView`/`setProgress`/`pause`/`resume`, one `Thread` field) is checked and `libmglnative` loaded on the main thread; any miss keeps the static layers. The render thread has no exception guard, so each thread it starts gets an uncaught handler that swaps the panel to the static layers instead of crashing SystemUI. The GL view is laid out at the shown size and counter-scaled, since mgl's buffer scale only applies once a surface exists, and it renders only while the panel is attached and visible. While the panel is held, the retention hook also rewrites switch-on shows and resends (`op 1`/`op 2`) to `op 3`: the island already exists, and the repost (about 0.5s after the torch lights, when the plugin's notification process cold-starts) only re-added the panel mid-drag. Pulling the island down opens the page through `EnterMiniWindow`; when the window has grown to full screen and is closed with back, the state machine dispatches `ExitApp`, which only restores `EnterApp` islands, so an after-hook on `DynamicIslandSafeguardsController.exitApp(String)` for the plugin package calls its own `exitMiniWindow(String)` when the flashlight island is still the package's main mini-window element. As a fallback, `DynamicIslandContentView.updateExpandedView(data, boolean, Continuation)` removes and re-adds the expanded view on every island update (torch on/off included), and the detach destroys the `TextureView` surface. So a before-hook on it, and the panel hiding for an expand or collapse, capture the revealed renderer's frame (`TextureView.getBitmap`). The read-back is synchronous on SystemUI's main thread at the start of a host transition, so it is half size, into one reused bitmap, and a second request within 150ms (a hide followed by its re-add) reuses the first. The new surface stays hidden behind that frame until `OnFirstFrameDrawListener` reports a drawn frame (re-armed through the renderer's first-frame flag on every attach), then fades in; the first open has no frame and fades in from black, as the page does. The fake copy shows the same frame, or, before one exists, the static layers with their beam alpha at the renderer's progress, so neither is brighter than the live panel. The session lights at the saved logical level (`mi_flashlight_strength`, the page's `getLogicStrength`), and ignores torch reports for 800ms after its own commands: switching on passes through the default level, and following that echo made the beam flash. The host stretches expanded content to `expandedViewMaxWidth` before measuring it, so a before-hook on `DynamicIslandBaseContentView.updateExpandedSize(int, int, DynamicIslandData)` passes the panel's own width and height for the flashlight data; the host clamps the width to 114..364dp, centres the island and sizes the fake view from the same values. The swap also sets `miui.focus.isPromoted` on the data extras, the only flag that lets the height pass `expanded_island_height_dp`, and restore writes the host value back. The beam layers fade on and off like the static effect, with alpha following the slider and the OpenGL page's 0.15 floor. Slider rules follow `MiFlashlightController`: progress 0..100 = start + vertical travel / slider height × 100, 0 switches off, the shown value follows `updateSeekBarProcess`, and haptics play only on reaching 0 or 100 and on the body tap, through `miui.util.HapticFeedbackUtil` (effect 4, then `"flick"`, then `View.performHapticFeedback(1)`). The page's switch Lottie is inflated as a plain `View` through a `LayoutInflater.Factory2`, because Lottie's async loader throws on the main thread when it fails; its touch strip is hidden. Any missing resource or id rejects the feature for the generation and the native card stays. Brightness uses the native page's channel: `Settings.Global mi_flashlight_strength` plus `ACTION_OPERATE_FLASHLIGHT` to SystemUI; readback is a `CameraManager.TorchCallback`. `DynamicIslandWindowView.dispatchTouchEvent` feeds every event to the window's press sink, drag-to-collapse and pull-to-full-screen gestures before any child sees it, so a before-hook takes a gesture whose down lands on the held panel's flashlight body (head width, from the head to the handle strip), dispatches it to the panel in panel coordinates and returns true; the window never sees it. Gestures starting on the beam or the handle strip stay with the island, so its press, collapse and pull-down to mini window / full screen keep working. In the panel a vertical drag moves the slider over the unscaled slider height (the page's `seekBarTouchLength`), a tap on the body toggles, and a horizontal-dominant move is ignored. Off state: while the panel is attached and visible (`FlashlightIslandHold.held`), a `handleFocusNotificationOrStatus(false, 0, user)` close becomes op 3 (status only); the panel sends the same `ACTION_TOGGLE_FLASHLIGHT` op 0 after it has been hidden or detached for 450 ms with the torch still off. Disable, plugin unload and hot reload put the native views back and call `updateDynamicIslandView(data, false)`; the controller crosses generations in `SystemUIPluginHooker` state (index 8). An upgrade from a build without the feature waits for the next flashlight island update. The full-screen page itself (`MiFlashlightActivity`) runs in the plugin's `miui.systemui.plugin:flashlight` process, which needs the `miui.systemui.plugin` scope (the Super Island page shows the missing-scope card for it and requests it when the panel is switched on). No close-position or `close_app_start` reaches SystemUI for it, so natively the page just fades and the island returns only after the window is gone. Back and the page's own bottom swipe (its "bottom draw up" gesture, what the gesture bar does on this page) both run `MiFlashlightManager.hideFlashlight()` → `MiFlashlightHideEvent` (the activity's `hideBgAnim`: blur progress 1→0 over ~420ms, mirrored into the layout alpha by the `onBgAnimUpdate` callback, then decor GONE and `finish()`) → `MiFlashlightLayout.hideView()`. The activity builds its layout with `needAnim=false`, so the layout's own Folme fade never runs there. `FlashlightPageExitHooker` hooks `hideView` before it runs. While the back torch is lit (a `TorchCallback` registered on the layout's attach and removed on its detach), the layout flies into the island over 380ms. It scales uniformly from the page centre (the flashlight head), with a rounded outline clip that narrows to a pill-shaped band around the head, stays opaque until 65% of the flight, then fades. During the flight `onBgAnimUpdate` gets a no-op callback, so the blur still fades natively but the layout alpha is ours. As the flight starts, the page sends `com.takekazex.hypertweak.action.FLASHLIGHT_PAGE_EXIT` to SystemUI as an ordered broadcast. The receiver requires `STATUS_BAR_SERVICE` from the sender, which the system-uid plugin holds; it is registered lazily and unregistered on hot reload. It calls `exitMiniWindow` for the parked flashlight island and answers with the island's screen bounds (content view X + `getBigIslandX()`, `getBigIslandViewWidth()`, `getIslandViewHeight()`). The flight starts at an estimate (cutout − 36dp … cutout + 9dp, the icon-only big island; height from `island_height`) and eases onto the answer, 35% of the gap per frame. `ExitMiniWindow` natively collapses with `MiniWindowToBigIsland`, a morph from the expanded geometry (for this island the 200×320dp panel, which read as a box). While our restore dispatches (500ms window, one-shot), a before-hook on `ResolveFromMiniWindowKt.resolveFromMiniWindow` replaces that for a `BigIsland` target that is not temp-hidden with the native `HiddenToBigIsland`, so the pill grows from the cutout while the page shrinks into it. The page opens through the window view directly, never through `DynamicIslandSafeguardsController.enterMiniWindow`, so the controller is captured from `delayDeleted(key, seconds)` on flashlight island updates and from `exitApp`. Within 3s of such an early restore, the native `exitApp` for the plugin is skipped, because its close-end state would run again on an island that is already back. Without the signal, the after-hook still restores the island once the page closes. Group `plugin.flashlight_page` delivers the switch to that process. `miui.systemui.plugin` is also loaded inside SystemUI, so force-stopping it kills SystemUI: `RestartScopeSelection.SHARED_WITH_SYSTEM_UI` keeps it out of the restart picker, `RestartUtils` and `RestartRootScript`.
- Control Center island hide (`ControlCenterSuperIslandHooker`). The host's combined `tempHidden` can stay false when only Control Center changes, so the hooker forces `isTempHiddenExt` and dispatches `onIslandTempHide` itself. Like the native `registerTempHiddenChanged` collector, it first calls `DynamicIslandWindowState.setTempHiddenChange(TRUE)`. `preHandleEvent` keeps that mark only for `IslandTempHiddenChanged`. Restores read it through `TransitionContext.isTempHiddenChange` and resolve `TempHiddenTo*`, whose `temp_hidden_to_show` → `showIslandLayout` → holder `onShow` resumes module animations (native Lottie, HyperSpectrum). Without the mark, a restore resolves as `BigIslandChanged`, and holders stay paused after `show_to_temp_hidden`.

## HyperOS media carousel

In the unlocked notification shade, the HyperOS style yields to the stock media row when the
host has sessions from a single app and profile and none are hidden or dismissed. Filtered
sessions keep the carousel in charge so the stock row cannot resurface a suppressed session.
The host owns its top session and the stock row remains bound throughout.

The pager keeps surviving native card views attached through session changes, cancels stale
page animations, and aligns the selected page after layout. The long-press modal temporarily
sets its source page invisible without changing its size. Dismissal restores visibility before
releasing modal resources. Pager movement, session membership changes and shade visibility
loss dismiss the modal.

## Notification-shade media switching

The OS4 media-card style uses the media-card live-settings group. An unset `media_card_carousel_style` reads the previous `media_card_swipe` switch, preserving existing AOSP selections. Style 0 uses the system single card, 1 uses AOSP, and 2 uses the HyperOS pager. The HyperOS pager reads MIUI's own sorted media candidates and creates one native `miui_media_session` view, MIUI binder, seek model and disposable coroutine scope per session. Each page includes the native media header and material binder, so shade glass, blur and normal backgrounds follow the host's material state. Pager layout synchronizes each nested header's `ExpandableView.actualHeight` so Android hit testing reaches its playback controls and card actions. The native Miuix page indicator follows the scroll position and is shown for multiple pages. Media touch uses the notification row's pressed scale. Long press binds a separate native media header and player in a full-screen status-bar sub-panel matching the native notification modal. It maps the pressed card through screen coordinates, moves the copy and action group together, and centers both using the native modal item spacing, collapsed notification height and bottom reserve. The original card is revealed again when the copy returns. A dedicated ModalWindowManager from the host factory drives the same blend blur, glass and solid fallback for this window without changing the stock row modal. The stock row modal itself requires a NotificationEntry. Close pauses the selected session and hides its card until playback resumes or the session ends. Hide app filters the current user's matching app only in this carousel. Restore hidden apps is available in the modal or directly in the media section when the filter leaves no pages. The filter is in memory and clears when leaving the HyperOS style or restarting SystemUI. Pages retain their order and selected identity across media updates and consume horizontal input through their own platform scroller. Each binder detaches and releases playback progress when its page disappears. AOSP remains a separate renderer. The notification header hosts SystemUI's Compose `Media` carousel, using the host factory and its media repository. When the legacy manager is active, its already-filtered user entries feed the Compose repository. The bridge releases only entries it published. The MIUI player stays available until the Compose view measures a nonzero area. The notification dismissal recognizer yields to the pager for touches that start in it, and stack scrolling uses the native vertical handler. Only the unlocked notification shade mounts this view. Disable and hot reload dispose the composition and restore the MIUI player. The control-center MiPlay card uses a separate plugin controller.

## Independent media Super Islands

The default-off `media_super_island_multi_session` preference is applied by the SystemUI island settings participant. SystemUI's current-user, active and dismissal-filtered media list supplies the candidates. The feature takes over when at least two cards are playing and keeps surviving cards registered until they stop. A session-owned task key namespaces the card notification key, while the host media instance ID deduplicates stale notification aliases. Each island has its own normal and animation holders, media binder, seek model, progress owner, and cancellable coroutine scope.

The native controller still consumes its top-media callbacks. During takeover its single-task add and remove are held, and the module invokes its native template builder with plugin lookup suspended on the main thread. The temporary controller fields are restored after each build. The plugin receives independently keyed adds and updates through the native content interface and arbitrates the normal island slots. The plugin's single pending media view reuse is skipped for these keys, so a newly added card cannot take over another card's animation view. A retired task is deleted without animation and releases its callbacks and seek observer. Disable and hot reload retire the feature-owned cards and resume the native publisher. The next generation recovers from the living Dagger component and the native media list, including an upgrade from a build without saved feature state.
